security_audit.summary: The high screen-capture detections are false positives: the skill asks for local app screenshot files and uses local DOM capture for export. The external-command detections are Markdown setup examples, inline code, or TypeScript snippets with fixed commands and no dynamic execution path. Manual review of mockup.png found a normal phone-frame PNG asset.

remediation.issue: Package-manager setup commands may modify the current project.
remediation.suggestion: State that scaffold and install commands require user confirmation before they run.

remediation.issue: The skill requests local app screenshots and an app icon from the user.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that assets should remain local unless the user explicitly chooses another workflow.

remediation.issue: The bundled mockup.png is a binary asset that static scanners cannot inspect deeply.
remediation.suggestion: Document the mockup source and keep the image hash stable between releases.

content.value_statement: App Store screenshots must sell the product quickly. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code build local generators for polished iOS marketing screenshots.
actual_capabilities: Plans an App Store screenshot narrative from user-provided features and brand inputs.
Guides setup of a local Next.js and Tailwind screenshot generator.
Uses a bundled iPhone mockup with measured screen overlay values.
Defines Apple portrait export sizes for modern iPhone screenshots.
Provides layout, typography, and copy rules for readable marketing slides.
Shows how to export PNG files with html-to-image from local browser previews.
limitations: It does not create App Store Connect listings or upload assets.
It depends on user-provided screenshots, icon files, colors, and feature details.
It focuses on iPhone portrait screenshots, not iPad or landscape formats.
It provides implementation guidance, not a ready hosted screenshot service.

use_cases.title: Prepare Launch Screenshots
use_cases.description: Turn product screenshots and brand details into a complete App Store screenshot plan and generator.

use_cases.title: Refresh Store Visuals
use_cases.description: Create new marketing slides when an app changes positioning, features, or visual identity.

use_cases.title: Automate Export Sizes
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable local workflow for previewing slides and exporting Apple-sized PNG files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My Screenshot Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an iOS App Store screenshot set for my app. Ask for the screenshots, icon, colors, font, features, slide count, and style.

prompt_templates.title: Write Slide Copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three headline options for each slide. Keep each headline short, readable at thumbnail size, and focused on one benefit.

prompt_templates.title: Build the Generator
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a local Next.js screenshot generator using my approved copy, screenshots, icon, colors, and the bundled phone mockup.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Exports
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the generator for export reliability. Verify sizing, image loading, font rendering, numbered filenames, and html-to-image behavior.

output_examples.input: A developer provides four app screenshots, an icon, blue brand colors, and a clean style request.
output: A four-slide narrative with hero, differentiator, feature, and trust screenshots.
A local preview page that shows every slide in a grid.
PNG exports sized for supported iPhone portrait resolutions.

output_examples.input: A designer wants stronger copy for a productivity app screenshot set.
output: Short headline options for each slide.
Recommendations for line breaks and visual rhythm.
A layout direction that varies phone position across slides.

output_examples.input: A team needs repeatable exports after every app release.
output: A local generator structure with reusable slide components.
A toolbar flow for previewing and downloading screenshots.
Numbered filenames that sort correctly after export.

best_practices: Approve the slide narrative and copy before building layouts.
Use real app screenshots and a high-resolution icon for final exports.
Run exports locally and review every PNG before App Store submission.
anti_patterns: Do not turn each slide into a dense feature list.
Do not reuse the same phone placement on every slide.
Do not upload private screenshots or icons to services the user did not approve.

faq.question: Does this skill upload my screenshots?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow uses local files and local browser export unless you add another service.

faq.question: What inputs do I need?
faq.answer: You need app screenshots, an app icon, brand colors, font preferences, feature priorities, slide count, and style direction.

faq.question: Can it make iPad screenshots?
faq.answer: The guidance focuses on iPhone portrait sizes. You can adapt the generator, but iPad layouts are not covered.

faq.question: Why does it use Next.js?
faq.answer: Next.js gives a local React page for precise layout, preview, and browser-based PNG export.

faq.question: Why is html-to-image recommended?
faq.answer: The skill says html-to-image handles complex CSS rendering better than html2canvas for this workflow.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
